chapter_theme: Ainkurunuru 301 to 310, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து, in which the friend tries to stop the man from crossing the waste for wealth: the road's flowers, its seized water, its starving elephant pair and its fires are set against the woman's grief, her slipping bangles and the smile of an unborn son.

301.reading: The friend tells the man of the dark-hilled country that if he crosses that range, where travellers on the hard waste crown their heads with the white clusters of the great pale lodhra, the woman he leaves will suffer greatly.
301.nuance: The only image of the road is a festive one: those who cross it wear its flowers on their heads. The friend grants the journey its attraction and sets against it a single plain clause about the one who stays; அவ்வரை, that range, is set against his own மைவரை, the dark hills he would leave.

thinai_evidence.note: a warning against a crossing of the waste that is still only intended

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

302.reading: The friend tells the man that his hard-won work for rare wealth has a right not to be failed, and the broad-shouldered woman has an equal right to hold him back; it would be good if he did not go, leaving her weeping and the rich place forlorn.
302.nuance: The two claims are set in matching lines (உரித்தே, உரியள்): she does not call the wealth-work wrong, only equal, and தகைத்தல், holding back, is the very act the decade is named for. She asks for a choice, not a verdict.

thinai_evidence.note: a departure for wealth that the friend tries to stop

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

303.reading: The friend asks the young man, since in summer's hard waste the banyan with fruit like new-fired pots holds back the போகில் bird, to take them with him so that the road may be cool and sweet.
303.nuance: Near miss for iraicchi: the banyan detaining the passing bird does what the decade wants done to the man, but lines 1 and 2 also carry the waste that line 3's wish (தண்ணிய இனிய வாக) refers to, so the deletion test does not plainly pass; it stays scene. The plea changes ground: not 'do not go' but 'go with us'.

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; எம்மொடும் makes the friend speak with the woman as 'us'

304.reading: The friend warns the young lord of strong horses that if he goes by the stony forking path, where the elephant seizes the cattle's water from the trough the unlettered herdsmen dug with their sticks, the soft woman with long cloud-dark hair will grieve; let him not be capable of it.
304.nuance: வல்லாதீமே asks him to be incapable: the strength his epithet praises (வயமான் தோன்றல்) is the strength the friend asks him to lack. The road's one water is dug by hand and still taken by force, so the waste is shown as a place where even what is made is lost.

thinai_evidence.note: the hero's intended crossing and the woman's grief

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

iraicchi.act: the tusker embraces his mate and, though starving, does not leave for other lands but suffers the hunger with her
iraicchi.sense: even the beast in drought will not leave his mate for a richer land, so the man who would leave her for wealth falls below it

305.reading: The friend asks the young man what gain his going will bring, if it makes the girl of bright bangles grieve, on the parched hills where the tusker, holding his mate close, does not wander to other lands but suffers with her as hunger eats them.
305.nuance: பிறபுலம் படராது is the exact negative of the hero's plan: the beast will not go to other lands even for food, the man will go to other lands for wealth. பயம், gain, is the hero's own measure turned against him.

thinai_evidence.note: hills whose green has dried, the waste of the hot season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

306.reading: The friend tells the warrior lord that if he crosses the wide waste, the dark woman with hair like a festival's abundance will grieve more than the flute laments, as the fine lines on her jewelled waist wither.
306.nuance: Her grief is measured against the flute (குழலினும்), the instrument of the evening's mourning music, so her lament is pictured as heard, not only felt. The address வெல்போர்க் குருசில் praises his victories in war just as it asks him not to set out.

thinai_evidence.note: an intended crossing and the grief it would cause

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

307.reading: The friend tells the lord of the shore that he has set his heart on the hill-bound hard waste where even the strong beast shies from the roaring flame of the fire-drill bamboo, and that his wealth is not good, since it comes by parting from his doll-like companion.
307.nuance: The beast fears the fire and the man does not fear the road, which the friend does not praise. The wealth is the grammatical subject that comes (வருமே) by the parting, so the parting is its price, paid by her. கொண்க, the shore-lord's address, is unusual in a paalai poem.

thinai_evidence.note: the hard waste of hills where fires blaze

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; நின் துணை names the woman as his wife

308.reading: The friend tells the man that it would be good not to part from the soft woman of thick dark hair; if he parts, they will part as one parts from the great hill where Murugan dwells and the bright blossoms of the eru tree lie strewn.
308.nuance: பிரிமே is first person plural: the friend speaks of the women's own parting, and the comparison is to leaving the sacred home hill, so his going would uproot them too. Whether this means leaving home with him, or leaving life, the poem does not settle.

thinai_evidence.note: the parting the friend tries to prevent

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

309.reading: The friend tells the man of the steep-hilled country that he is set on crossing the hot waste in the summer month, and asks whether the wealth he would make by going is sweeter than seeing the smile of the little son his loving wife carries in her heavy pregnancy.
309.nuance: The son is not yet born (கடுஞ்சூல்), so the smile weighed against the wealth is one he has never seen; the friend sets made wealth (செய் பொருள்) against a good that needs only his presence. நன்று in line 2 is ironic.

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; கடுஞ்சூல் places the poem in married life

310.reading: The friend tells the young man that if he is capable of parting, so that the bright bangles of her soft shoulders and her ornaments slip loose, the beauty of her fine brow will be hard to keep.
310.nuance: Her body is described first by its ornaments (the gold girdle of coins, the bangles) and the harm is told as their loosening, the visible sign of wasting. வல்லுவை, 'if you are able', makes the departure a test of his hardness, not of his means.

thinai_evidence.note: the parting and the wasting it would cause

links.note: Kural 1151 refuses any promise of quick return and asks only whether he is leaving; Ainkurunuru 302 grants that his work for wealth has its own right and argues only that the woman has an equal one.
links.teaches: Read together they show the friend's dissuasion in two registers, the couplet's flat ultimatum of death and the poem's balanced concession of rights, so the Kural's line is an extreme the Sangam friend reaches only after first admitting the claim of wealth.

links.note: Both use the elephant pair shrinking together in hunger on the scorched hill; in Akananuru 91 the friend uses it after he has gone to comfort the woman, in Ainkurunuru 305 before he goes to shame the man out of going.
links.teaches: The same image of the starving pair that will not part is turned on the man as reproach before the journey and on the woman as reassurance after it, so in the convention one karu image carries opposite arguments depending on whether the departure is still preventable.

links.note: Kural 64 makes the gruel stirred by children's small hands sweeter than amrita; Ainkurunuru 309 asks whether wealth gained across the waste is sweeter than an unborn son's smile.
links.teaches: The couplet's household ranking of children above every delicacy becomes, in the friend's mouth, a direct argument against the wealth journey, showing that the Kural's measure of sweetness was already a tool for weighing a husband's absence against his family.

links.note: In both the friend tells the man who has announced his journey that the woman's bangles will slip; Akananuru 271 wishes his work be capable (வல்வதாக) and asks if there is medicine for her, Ainkurunuru 310 asks whether he is capable (வல்லுவை) of parting.
links.teaches: Both friends turn வல், the capacity a man needs for his work, into the hardness that parting demands, so the pair shows the dissuasion convention attacking the hero's prized strength itself rather than his reasons for going.

source_issues: 301-310: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; every speaker and addressee in thurai_akam (the friend to the departing man) is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poems, so occasion words are null.
302: line 4 மல்லம் புலம்ப is obscure (perhaps மல்லல் அம், the rich place, grieving); the reading of the closing line turns on it.
306: பல்கழ் in line 2 (perhaps பல்காழ், many strands of beads) and விழவொலி கூந்தல் in line 4 are hard to fix; the reading of the woman's ornaments and hair is uncertain.
308: the sense of பிரிந்தெனப் பிரிமே (who parts, and from what) is not settled by the text.
